description: Somos estudantes no Centro de Informática da UFPE, e nos interessamos pelo tema por saber o quão difícil é fazer crianças e adolescentes se interessarem pela ciência, justamente pela forma a qual aprendem. Pensando assim, escolhemos o desafio, e tentamos tornar o aprendizado divertido.
summary:
This stage-based space survival simulator challenges you to plan and execute a complex lunar mission, emphasizing realism and resource management.
The journey begins with spacecraft assembly, serving as an organic tutorial. You must include mandatory modules but can customize with extras. However, adding modules dynamically alters ship efficiency and travel time, which factors in the exact arrival.
Upon landing, your first task is organizing the base. The game then unfolds through successive stages featuring embedded mini-games that simulate astronaut routines: exploration, mining, equipment repairs, and material crafting.
You will face real-world hazards like solar storms and abrasive lunar dust. Beyond technical maintenance, you must manage the human element—monitoring hunger, energy, and physical exhaustion, while dealing with the psychological toll of deep loneliness.
Every decision leads to one of several endings: achieving mission success by completing all stages, failing if the character succumbs to starvation or exhaustion, or actively choosing to give up the mission.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Our project is a stage-based space survival and exploration simulator. It works by following the entire journey of a lunar mission. It begins with spacecraft assembly, which acts as an organic tutorial: the player manages mandatory and extra modules, dynamically visualizing how their choices alter efficiency and exact travel time. Upon landing, the player must organize the base and perform routine astronaut tasks through embedded mini-games (exploration, mining, equipment repairs, and material crafting).

What benefits does it offer and what is the intended impact?

The game offers an immersive experience in decision-making and critical resource management. Additionally, it offers a sense of personalization and belonging, giving players the ability to create avatars they identify with, which facilitates immersion and interest. The intended impact is to educate and raise awareness among players about the extreme technical, environmental, and, above all, psychological difficulties involved in space colonization and survival off-Earth.

What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use?

To develop Lunar Base Junior, we used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the game, along with NASA APIs to integrate real space-related data and resources:

  • NASA DONKI API – Space weather events.
  • NASA TechPort API – NASA technology projects.
  • NASA Image and Video Library API – Real images from space missions.

What is the creative aspect of your project?

The most creative aspect is the deep integration of the "human element" in contrast to technical maintenance. The environment is unforgiving with real-world hazards (solar storms, lunar dust), but the player does not just manage machines; they must take care of the character's hunger, physical exhaustion, and mental health, dealing with profound feelings of loneliness.

What factors did your team consider?

Our team strongly considered player autonomy and the consequences of their choices. Because of this, we implemented multiple realistic endings: the player can achieve success by completing all stages, fail if the astronaut succumbs to starvation and exhaustion, or even choose to give up the mission due to the psychological and physical toll of the journey.
